sections.name: File setup, idempotencyKey
sections.title: Imports and the event key
sections.what: Brings in the scoring rules, the error type and the data functions, and defines the unique key for each scoring event.
sections.why: The key makes re-running a score safe, because the same match, team, player and version always give the same key.
sections.watch_out: Changing the key format breaks duplicate detection for matches already scored.

sections.name: scoreMatch
sections.title: Score a finished match
sections.what: Checks the match exists, reads each player's stat line, works out points for every team's picks including captain and vice captain adjustments, saves them and reports how many were new. Throws clear errors for a missing match or a bad stat line.
sections.why: Points come from the real scorecard, because the input rules forbid made-up points. The captain and vice captain rule itself lives in the scoring library and is not shown here.
sections.watch_out: A player with no stat line gives zero points with no warning.

summary: Scores a finished match from its real scorecard into the append-only ledger, and running it again adds nothing new.
purpose: Turns per-player stat lines into points for each fantasy team without ever inventing points.
why: The file header says scoring is idempotent, and the input rules forbid generated points.
how: Checks the match exists, parses each player's stat line, builds one scoring row per picked player for every team, saves them through the repo, and reports the counts.
inputs: A match id and per-player stat lines, plus a scoring version that defaults to the current one.
outputs: A result with team count, events written, events already present, and the scoring version.
risks: A player with no stat line is silently skipped, so a missing scorecard entry gives zero points without a warning. Bad stat lines stop the whole run.
debug: Read the error message: it names the bad player for an invalid stat line, or says the match was not found. Compare the stat keys with the parser in the scoring library.
